title: Tukar, the team
note: The team presentation. Every picture is a Playwright recording of a real public page, and every box is drawn where capture.mjs measured the element it points at. Facts are limited to what the pages show and what docs/SCF_SUBMISSION.md already states.

scenes.vo: Hi, I'm Pugar Huda Mantoro, and I am the whole team behind Tukar, a private remittance corridor on Stellar. This is who is building it, and why the build can be trusted.
I build in public. Over a hundred repositories and thousands of contributions in the past year, and most of them are products you can open, not experiments.
Several were judged well. Diam took first at the iExec Vibe Coding Challenge, the Portaldot developer kit took first, Brownie to Ape took second, and KasPay was a community choice at Kaspathon.
The closest prior work is Segel, a sealed-bid OTC desk on Stellar. Same chain and same proof stack as Tukar: Circom and Groth16 on BN254, verified on-chain by Soroban.
Private settlement is the thread through most of my work: Bisik on Canton, Senyap on Midnight, Diam on iExec, and Sealed Pair on Sui.
Compliance is the other half. Amanah pairs zero-knowledge KYC with proof of reserves, across ten contracts on Casper testnet.

boxes.label: ZK KYC and proof of reserves

scenes.vo: Utuh is a completeness layer: it bonds that nothing was left out of an attestation. That is the same question Tukar's audit requests work on.
Tukar itself placed fifth in Stellar Hacks: Real-World ZK, and was a Grand Finalist at Stellar APAC, in payments and consumer applications.
All of it is open source: fifteen Soroban contracts, eight circuits, and three hundred thirty-three passing contract tests.
What I have not done yet is scale a product to real users. That is the honest gap, and the plan buys in the operational specialists for it. Private in the middle, accountable at the edges.

boxes.label: Private in the middle, accountable at the edges
